title:
Abandoned but
Not Forgotten
subtitle:
Every object has a story.
Even the ones a world away.
welcome: Hello, explorer! I’m Pip. Ready to discover the stories we left among the stars?
footer: No rush. Space has been waiting for you.
turn: Click a corner or drag to turn the page
storyTitle: It started with a little dream.
storyIntro: One evening, Ari looked up at the Moon and wondered…
thought: Has anyone ever left something up there?
speech: Oh, yes! And every little thing has a big story.
storyEnd: Follow Ari and Pip across the Moon. Meet the machines that helped us explore—and discover why they stayed behind.
mapIntro: Spin the Moon. Tap a glowing point to find its story.
mapNote: One small discovery at a time.
lockedHint: This story is still being written! Explore the lunar rover in this prototype.
missionIntro: In 1971, Apollo 15 brought an electric car to the Moon. Astronauts could explore farther than ever before.
missionComic: No roads. No petrol. Just a whole new world to explore!
missionEnd: When the astronauts flew home, there wasn’t room for their rover. It stayed behind—along with its tracks and an incredible story.
whatAnswer: A battery-powered car made for astronauts on the Moon.
whyAnswer: The trip home had a weight limit. Moon rocks came home; the rover stayed.
scienceAnswer: Longer journeys, more samples, and a closer look at lunar geology.
puzzleIntro: Our spacecraft can carry 12 kg home. Bring the science samples and memories. The rover can stay on the Moon.
gentle: Try bringing the rocks and film home, and leaving the heavy equipment. You can move any item again!
success: Beautiful packing! You brought discoveries home and left a story on the Moon.
drag: Drag an item, or tap it then choose a destination.
memoryIntro: Your collection of stories from a world away.
empty: A passport is waiting for you. Discover the rover to add it here.
badgeText: Collected a story and packed for Earth.
saved: Your discoveries are saved on this device.
hintStory: Look closely! The rover’s tracks have no wind or rain to wash them away.
hintPuzzle: Science samples are small, but their discoveries are big!
